newsitem.title: USA: Motorola gets $25 million iDEN contract.
newsitem.headline: Motorola gets $25 million iDEN contract.

text.p: Motorola Inc's Land Mobile Products Sector said Friday it received a $25 million equipment order from Infocom Communications Network Inc, a wireless communications provider in the Philippines.
Motorola said it will provide Infocom with an iDEN (Integrated Digital Enhanced Network) communications system. The order was placed in December 1996.
Infocom earlier this year was granted a 25-year license by the Philippine government to provide wireless services throughout the nation, Motorola said.
The iDEN system gives users dispatch capabilities including instant conferencing and wireless intercom, telephone interconnection, a short message service similar to paging, among other things.

Plans call for the service to initially be available in metropolitan Manila during the third quarter of 1997. When first installed, the network will have the capacity to serve about 38,000 subscribers. System capacity is expected to grow to more than 100,000 by the year 2000, Motorola said.

According the Motorola, McCaw International Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Nextel Communications Inc, last year purchased a 30 percent interest in Infocom. Nextel is deploying iDEN technology in the United States.
Infocom currently operates a nationwide paging business in the Philippines.
Motorola provides wireless communications, semiconductors, and advanced electronic systems and services.
